newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Lippo Securities ready for retail boom.
newsitem.headline: Lippo Securities ready for retail boom.

text.p: Indonesia's large PT Lippo Securities brokerage house says it is well-placed to exploit a retail explosion in the domestic securities industry.
"Our brokerage volume has tripled to 5.3 trillion rupiah ($2.3 billion) following a strong push into domestic retail," president-director Charles de Queljoe told Reuters.
Lippo's brokerage volume soared 299 percent to 5.32 trillion rupiah in the first nine months of 1996, with 35 percent coming from local retail investors, he said.
"In the first nine months of last year we posted 1.33 trillion rupiah in brokerage volume, with the local retail investors contributing almost nothing," de Queljoe said.

De Queljoe said the firm's brokerage volume growth of 299 percent in the first nine months of this year against the same period last year had out-performed the significant volume growth of 114 percent on the Jakarta Stock Exchange itself.

Total exchange volume had risen to 48.13 trillion rupiah in the first nine months against 22.49 trillion rupiah in the same period last year partly because of a surge in domestic retail participation, he said.
Domestic investors currently account for only around 30 percent of the exchange's trading volume, while the rest came from foreign players, de Queljoe said.

"Eventually, I think, this market will be very similar to what you see today in Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore or Hong Kong where domestic investors account for a large portion of the total market volume," he said.
He said Indonesia offered opportunities for significant growth as there were only between 300,000-400,000 local investors against a total population of nearly 200 million.
De Queljoe said there were around 30 million middle class Indonesians earning $3,000 or more per month which could offer a very attractive market for brokerage firms.
The recent successful listing of the giant state-owned Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) was partly due to capitalising on the strength of domestic retail investors, he said.
He said Lippo Securities expected to have a larger network to further boost its domestic investors base following a recent 875 billion rupiah restructuring within the conglomerate Lippo Group.
The group announced in September a plan under which Lippo Securities has taken an additional 27 percent stake in insurance firm Lippo Life to raise its holding to 32 percent.
Lippo Life has boosted its holding in Lippo Bank to 45 percent with the purchase of an additional 40 percent stake.
"Ultimately, what we want to achieve through this network is that we will be able to be almost everywhere in Indonesia.
"Wherever there is a Lippo Life or Lippo Bank branch, theoritically Lippo Securities can have a representative who could simply execute buy and sell orders," de Queljoe said.
Lippo Life and Lippo Bank together have about 1.7 million individual customers and that was a key target market for Lippo Securities, he said.
